title: First French colonial empire
capsule: The First French colonial empire as constituted under Napoleon's Empire (1805–1815) was a drastically reduced remnant of France's pre-revolutionary overseas holdings: Saint-Domingue had been lost to the Haitian Revolution (1804) after the destruction of an army of 55,000, Louisiana was sold to the United States in 1803, and British naval superiority had captured or blockaded most remaining possessions. The rump empire consisted primarily of scattered Caribbean islands (Guadeloupe, Martinique), French Guiana, Réunion, and minor Indian Ocean and West African footholds. After Napoleon's defeat the Congress of Vienna (1814–1815) permanently ceded Mauritius, the Seychelles, Saint Lucia, and Tobago to Britain, leaving France with token overseas territories until the second colonial empire commenced with the conquest of Algeria in 1830.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The surviving colonial territories of 1805–1815 are historically documented, but reconstructing precise territorial polygons for this rump empire is problematic given dispersed island holdings and contested occupation during the Napoleonic Wars.
